projects.title: Scalable Constitutional AI + RLHF Fine-Tuning Pipeline
projects.summary: Build an end-to-end post-training pipeline on a small open-source base model that implements supervised fine-tuning, a reward model, RLHF (PPO or DPO), and a Constitutional AI-style critique-and-revision loop, then scale it to multi-GPU distributed training with reproducibility tooling. This is the most direct evidence you can implement, scale, and productionize the exact alignment techniques the role centers on.

components.name: RLHF + Constitutional AI core pipeline
components.description: A pipeline that takes a base model through SFT, trains a reward model on preference data, runs RLHF (PPO or DPO), and adds a constitutional critique-revision self-improvement stage where the model critiques and rewrites its own outputs against a written 'constitution' before further preference training.
components.rationale: Implementing the full CAI+RLHF stack end-to-end, including translating the CAI critique-revision idea into working training code, directly demonstrates the ability to scale and productionize these specific research techniques.

components.name: Distributed multi-GPU scale-up
components.description: Port the single-GPU pipeline to multi-GPU (and ideally multi-node) execution using FSDP or DeepSpeed, with measured throughput/memory benchmarks showing the scaling behavior and bottlenecks as GPU count increases.
components.rationale: Concrete before/after scaling numbers on real distributed hardware are direct evidence of comfort with large-scale distributed training infrastructure.

components.name: Reproducibility layer
components.description: Versioned experiment configs, fixed seeds and data manifests, and structured experiment tracking (e.g., via a logging tool) so that any run can be exactly reproduced and compared against prior runs.
components.rationale: A working system where any historical run can be re-executed to identical results is direct proof of establishing reproducible practices, not just a claim of caring about them.

components.name: Research-to-production playbook
components.description: A written record documenting the messy exploratory phase (failed hyperparameters, unstable reward signals, ablations) alongside the final hardened, tested pipeline, showing the decision points where exploration was cut off in favor of engineering rigor.
components.rationale: Showing the actual before/after of turning exploratory experiments into a disciplined pipeline is concrete evidence of balancing research freedom with engineering rigor, rather than an assertion of the skill.

roadmap.milestone: Baseline SFT + reward model + RLHF/DPO loop on a small open model, single GPU
Add Constitutional AI critique-revision stage on top of the RLHF loop
Scale to multi-GPU/multi-node with FSDP or DeepSpeed and benchmark throughput/memory
Add versioned configs, seed/data manifests, and experiment tracking
Write the research-to-production playbook documenting the exploration-to-rigor transition

projects.title: Post-Training Evaluation and Debugging Toolkit
projects.summary: Build a suite of evaluation and diagnostic tools that sit alongside any fine-tuning pipeline: a multi-dimension eval harness, automated anomaly detection for common training pathologies, and a bisection tool that pinpoints which data, hyperparameter, or checkpoint change caused a behavioral regression. This project emphasizes measurement and debugging depth rather than training-technique breadth.

components.name: Multi-dimensional eval harness
components.description: An evaluation suite scoring model checkpoints across several axes at once (task capability, instruction-following, refusal/harmlessness behavior on a safety probe set, and output format consistency), producing a single comparable report per checkpoint.
components.rationale: A working harness that quantifies multiple quality dimensions simultaneously is direct evidence of building the kind of measurement tooling the role asks for, rather than relying on a single benchmark score.

components.name: Training anomaly detector
components.description: Instrumentation that watches a live training run for known pathologies — reward hacking signatures, gradient norm spikes, KL-divergence blowups, loss plateaus — and flags them automatically during or after a run.
components.rationale: An automated detector that catches real pathological training behavior on your own runs is concrete proof of the ability to diagnose complex training issues, not just describe them.

components.name: Regression bisection tool
components.description: A tool that takes two checkpoints with different eval results and walks back through the intermediate data batches, hyperparameter changes, or code diffs between them to localize which change caused the behavior shift, packaged so it could plug into any team's existing pipeline.
components.rationale: Bisection tooling that pinpoints the root cause of a specific regression is strong evidence of debugging skill, and framing it as a pluggable tool shows the translate-research-into-usable-infrastructure mindset.

components.name: Per-checkpoint eval dashboard
components.description: A dashboard that plots the multi-dimensional eval results and anomaly flags over the course of training, so quality tradeoffs across checkpoints are visible at a glance.
components.rationale: Turning raw eval numbers into a usable dashboard demonstrates the tooling is built to actually improve model performance decisions, not just log data.

roadmap.milestone: Build the multi-dimensional eval harness and run it against a handful of checkpoints
Add automated anomaly detection instrumentation to a live training run
Build the bisection tool and demonstrate it localizing a deliberately introduced regression
Wire eval results and anomaly flags into a per-checkpoint dashboard

projects.title: Reliable Fine-Tuning Infrastructure with Incident Drills
projects.summary: Build the operational backbone around a fine-tuning job rather than the training technique itself: fault-tolerant multi-node execution, monitoring/alerting, and rehearsed incident response. This project emphasizes the on-call, systems-reliability side of the role for candidates whose strongest signal is infrastructure and operations rather than research technique novelty.

components.name: Fault-tolerant distributed training job
components.description: A multi-GPU (ideally multi-node) fine-tuning job with automatic checkpointing and elastic restart, so that a killed worker or preempted node resumes training without losing significant progress.
components.rationale: Demonstrating a training job that survives real node/worker failure on distributed hardware is direct evidence of large-scale systems competence beyond just launching a multi-GPU job.

components.name: Training monitoring and alerting stack
components.description: Metrics and alerting (e.g., via Prometheus/Grafana or a lightweight equivalent) tracking throughput, GPU utilization, loss trajectory, and hardware health, configured to page on the kinds of failures that would need urgent attention.
components.rationale: A working alerting pipeline that pages on real failure conditions is the closest a solo portfolio project can get to demonstrating on-call readiness for urgent operational incidents.

components.name: Chaos drills and incident runbooks
components.description: Deliberately injected failures (killed nodes, OOM, corrupted data shards) run against the pipeline, with written runbooks for triage and a postmortem for each drill describing root cause and time-to-resolution.
components.rationale: Practicing and documenting rapid triage under simulated failure conditions is concrete, verifiable evidence of composure and skill in exactly the short-notice debugging scenarios the role calls out.

components.name: Infra-as-code reproducible environment
components.description: The entire training/monitoring stack defined as code (container images, cluster config, environment pinning) so the whole setup can be torn down and rebuilt identically.
components.rationale: An environment that can be rebuilt byte-for-byte from code is evidence of reproducibility at the infrastructure layer, complementing experiment-level reproducibility.

roadmap.milestone: Stand up a multi-GPU/multi-node fine-tuning job with checkpoint/restart fault tolerance
Add a monitoring and alerting stack around the training job
Run chaos drills against the pipeline and write runbooks/postmortems for each
Package the full stack as infra-as-code for one-command rebuild
